title: Perturbation Effects on Robustness and Individual Fairness

problem.claim: Deep neural networks can experience simultaneous degradation of prediction robustness and individual fairness under adversarial perturbations.

gap.claim: Existing evaluation protocols typically assess robustness and fairness in isolation, obscuring critical failure modes.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes Robust Individual Fairness (RIF), requiring predictions under semantic-preserving perturbations to remain correct with respect to ground truth and invariant across semantically equivalent individuals.
The paper introduces RIFair, a black-box adversarial framework using a decoupled perturbation strategy to construct semantically preserved instance pairs that are unrobust and/or unfair.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across multiple model architectures and real-world textual datasets reportedly show that robustness-only or fairness-only metrics often miss Robust Biased and Unrobust Fair behaviors.
The authors report that RIFair reliably exposes hidden vulnerabilities and support RIF as a necessary criterion for trustworthy model assessment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Adversarial perturbations can jointly harm robustness and individual fairness.
Separate evaluation of robustness and fairness can hide important failure modes.
RIF defines a joint requirement of correctness and invariance under semantic-preserving perturbations.
RIFair operationalizes RIF assessment through black-box, decoupled adversarial perturbations.
Reported experiments identify behaviors missed by single-dimension metrics, and the framework exposes these vulnerabilities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architectures or textual datasets used.

The perturbation construction and evaluation procedures are not detailed.
